title: eCPRI: Use dissector table to parse payload
description: Make it possible to define alternative dissectors for eCPRI payload

notes.body:
So oran_fh_cus will still be the default dissector if no plugin takes its place?
This might make accessing the built-in dissector *slightly* slower now that every frame will involve checking a table?

I would encourage you to feed any bug fixes or enhancements you can back to packet-oran.c.  If there are design changes (within reason) that would make it easier for you to stay closer to it, do let me know.  I try to add new sections/extensions/fields soon after standards are released, but may miss them, or in some cases initially add them blind or from frames written/extended using scapy.

> So oran_fh_cus will still be the default dissector if no plugin takes its place?

Yes, that was my intension. But, I could not find a way to make it "pre-selected" by default. In a fresh start, without any saved preferences, you need to do "Decode as" and select "O-RAN FH CUS" as the only option. See my last comment in my previous merge request (https://gitlab.com/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/22990#note_2991028443)

> This might make accessing the built-in dissector _slightly_ slower now that every frame will involve checking a table?

Good point!  Now they are dissected by `dissector_try_payload_with_data()` compared to `call_dissector_only()` as before.  Maybe there's a way to look up the dissector handle only when it is changed, cache it and call using `call_dissector_only()` ?

Anyway, the only reason for me to submit this merge request was to make it possible to override the "O-RAN FH CUS" dissector, I am not so sure anymore that it was such a good idea .... I'll let you decide, no harm from my side if this one is rejected.

Thanks for maintaining and updating this dissector, I will report any findings back to you and the community.

I actually think something closer to your original MR might be more appropriate.  So have a dissector name, but an empty string would effectively be the default of "oran_fh_cus" ?

@mmann78 - would that be OK for you?

I'm always after consistency, but that can be difficult sometimes with how flexible Wireshark's code is (and how some developers choose to apply it). I guess I'm still in the camp of "If you want to dynamically change how a 'following payload' is dissected, it should be done with Decode As and not buried in/tied to a specific protocol".  Since this MR was created, I did stumble across a few other dissectors that have the "next payload dissector as a string" preference and I wanted to rip it out immediately (again for _consistency_ to our users), but it would break some backwards compatibility.  That's why I'm trying to get this MR to use Decode As (with a dissector table) because I think it's the right design architecturally.

In this case, the built-in oran-fh-cus dissector is the standard one most people will expect to be called, and I wouldn't be happy if I or anyone else had to do anything to ensure that it gets called by default.

I am aware of internal alternatives to the standard protocol, and competing proposals for upcoming features (I've done temporary internal extensions for some of these). As I said, I'd be prepared to consider reworking the dissector a little to make it easier for people to plug in their own extensions if:
- it doesn't make it too ugly or difficult to use or work on the main dissector
- it increases the likelihood that these changes, once proven or standardized, get contributed back

There probably should be a `dissector_add_payload` function or something else to set the default handle of a payload FT_NONE table (or pass it in when creating it). `dissector_add_uint` with 0 would work except it would throw a DISSECTOR ASSERT currently.

I agree with @martin.r.mathieson, that in this case my original MR (https://gitlab.com/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/22990) is more appropriate and less intrusive.

For the vast majority of the users (including myself - most of the time), "oran_fh_cus" is the only dissector of interest to parse an eCPRI payload. But occasionally I want to override it with something else, which is not possible with the current state of things.

The dissector table approach is of course _the_ elegant way of handling an open-ended transport protocol, but I think this is a different use case: The only thing I'm after is to _be able_ to override the default payload dissector without the need to make a special patched build of Wireshark.

In my opinion, this openness of Wireshark (possibility to write your own dissectors) is one of its strongest points and a killer feature.

Again, thanks to all of you for maintaining this wonderful piece of SW and @mmann78 I truly respect your care for architecture and consistency.
